analysis.AN_Notes: Survey and taxonomy of intersectional fairness notions (subgroup, calibration-based, metric-based, differential, max-min, probabilistic) and mitigation (with and without demographics), plus NLP, ranking and auditing applications. Bias axes structure the synthesis through intersectional groups of gender and race (e.g. Black women); disability, socioeconomic status and others appear only in reported studies. Harm types structure the synthesis as fairness notions: outcome parity in decisions with the disparate-impact four-fifths rule extended by differential fairness (Indirect_Discrimination) and worst-case accuracy or loss across subgroups (Disparate_Performance). Mitigation stages synthesised: in-processing (DRO, adversarial reweighting, auditor-learner game), post-processing (multicalibration boosting, multiaccuracy post-processing, prediction flipping) and stakeholder involvement and auditing (Organisational_Process). Evaluated refers to synthesised experimental results of the reviewed methods (adversarial reweighting and Pareto approaches improve fairness for some intersectional groups; independent-group debiasing prone to gerrymandering), not to an experiment of the survey itself.
